resources.string: LUPita needs these permissions to work. They are only used on this device.
Lets the floating bubble be drawn on top of any app.
It is the only way to turn the bubble off: without it there would be no way to close it.
Which apps are read, security measures and exceptions
What LUPita reads and how to turn it on
LUPita needs the accessibility service to read the text of the area you choose. Before you turn it on, here is what it does and what it does not:
Reads the text and structure of the app you have open.
Only when you confirm a capture, and only for the area you drew.
Never reads or captures anything from apps you mark as protected.
Never includes password fields, in any app.
Nothing is saved raw on its own: only what you decide.
What is read may be sent to the AI provider you choose for analysis, with the safety filters on.
You can review and change each measure in Privacy and security.
You decide which apps LUPita may read and how carefully. Nothing raw is stored, and only what you choose leaves the device.
Changes apply from the next capture.
Nothing is read or captured from this app.
Only the chosen area, with a preview and without keeping the text.
Only the chosen area; the result is saved.
Those that are in no list. Recommended: Sensitive.
Applies a sensitivity level to each app. If you turn it off, everything is treated as normal.
Password fields on screen are never included.
For sensitive apps, shows exactly what will be sent and asks for confirmation.
Replaces cards, IBANs, emails, phone numbers and IDs with markers. It is a safety net: it does not catch everything.
Keeps only metadata (time, app, tool and size) of what leaves the device.
Suggests protecting unknown apps whose name looks like banking or passwords.
Turn on the app lists of each region.
Change the level of a whole group at once.
You have not added any yet. An exception always beats the lists.
The analyses you run will appear here, with their date, the captured area and the tools used.
